change_interpretations.engineering_summary: The positive torque response time limit after accelerator pedal demand exceeds 70% has been relaxed from 100 ms to 120 ms. Test procedures and script pass criteria asserting 100 ms limits must be updated to align with the relaxed threshold.

assessments.reason: This test directly verifies VCU-DR-01 by testing 75% pedal demand against a 100 ms response threshold. Since VCU-DR-01 relaxed the limit to 120 ms, the test procedure and automated script threshold (currently 100 ms) must be updated.
evidence: Procedure: confirm requested positive torque no later than 100 ms
assessments.recommended_action: Update the script threshold and test procedure limit from 100 ms to 120 ms to reflect the revised VCU-DR-01 requirement.

assessments.reason: The test applies 85% pedal demand which triggers VCU-DR-01 conditions alongside brake arbitration, but previous evidence did not record timing measurements. It is unclear if the torque response timing was evaluated or needs re-verification under the relaxed 120 ms limit.
evidence: Comment: Timing not reported in old evidence
assessments.recommended_action: Re-run the test with response timing logging enabled to confirm compliance with the revised VCU-DR-01 requirement.

assessments.reason: The test procedure evaluates pedal demand steps (75–95%) matching VCU-DR-01 behavior, but uses a legacy check of 95 ms tolerance. Although the requirement link was lost during migration, the test threshold must be updated to align with the new 120 ms limit.
evidence: Comment: Legacy suite still checks 95 ms tolerance
Workshop note: High-load campaign did not keep all requirement hyperlinks after migration
assessments.recommended_action: Restore the requirement link to VCU-DR-01 and update the legacy suite tolerance check from 95 ms to 120 ms.

assessments.reason: This test measures emergency brake command latency under VCU-BRK-03, which is unchanged. Workshop notes explicitly clarify that brake latency uses a different clock and must not be conflated with driver torque response time.
evidence: Procedure: Trigger emergency brake alone; target brake command latency within 100 ms
Workshop note: Brake command latency and positive torque command latency are measured by different clocks
assessments.recommended_action: No action required; retain existing test procedure and baseline evidence.

assessments.reason: The test verifies diagnostic logging and degraded mode entry upon wheel-speed sensor failure per unchanged requirement VCU-DGN-04.
evidence: Procedure: Unplug simulated wheel-speed sensor and confirm degraded mode + fault log

assessments.reason: This test verifies operating mode event logging under unchanged requirement VCU-LOG-05.
evidence: Procedure: Change Comfort to Sport; log timestamp and build identifier

assessments.reason: The test exercises 80% pedal demand, which relates to VCU-DR-01, but has a TBD requirement link, unclear ownership, and has never been run. Traceability and applicability must be resolved by the owner.
evidence: Procedure: At 80% pedal and elevated load...
Comment: Ownership and source link to be clarified
assessments.recommended_action: Assign a definitive owner to clarify the requirement link and determine if this test should evaluate VCU-DR-01 response timing.

assessments.reason: The test links to VCU-OLD-88, an unknown requirement from a legacy catalog, making traceability broken.
evidence: Comment: Imported row; requirements catalog changed
assessments.recommended_action: Review legacy requirement VCU-OLD-88 with system engineering to remap or retire this test case.

assessments.reason: This test checks torque ramp shape comparisons between Sport and Comfort modes under VCU-MOD-06 without enforcing a quantitative response time limit.
The test evaluates pedal signal spike filtering under unchanged requirement VCU-DR-02 and does not check torque latency.
evidence: Procedure: Inject 7 ms false pedal pulse...

assessments.reason: This test verifies torque override priority during emergency braking under unchanged requirement VCU-BRK-03.
evidence: Procedure: While demand is high, request emergency braking and verify positive torque drops according to brake priority

assessments.reason: This test evaluates ECU power-up startup timing (500 ms readiness), which is unrelated to driver torque response time.
evidence: Procedure: Power cycle the ECU; verify readiness within 500 ms
